definitions.explanation: The part of the arm between the shoulder and the elbow, often a focus of fitness and beauty discussions in Japanese.

examples.japanese: {二|に}の{腕|うで}を{細|ほそ}くしたい。
examples.english: I want to slim down my upper arms.

examples.japanese: {二|に}の{腕|うで}のたるみが{気|き}になる。
examples.english: I'm concerned about the sagging of my upper arms.

examples.japanese: {二|に}の{腕|うで}を{鍛|きた}えるエクササイズ。
examples.english: Exercises to tone the upper arms.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: {二|に}の{腕|うで} literally means "second arm," historically referring to the upper arm as opposed to the forearm ({前腕|ぜんわん}). In older Japanese, {一|いち}の{腕|うで} referred to the forearm.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{二|に}の{腕|うで}のたるみ (upper arm flab/sagging)
・{二|に}の{腕|うで}を{引|ひ}き{締|し}める (to tone the upper arms)
・{二|に}の{腕|うで}のダイエット (diet/exercise for upper arms)
・{二|に}の{腕|うで}が{太|ふと}い (thick upper arms)
・{二|に}の{腕|うで}シェイプ (upper arm shaping)

BODY IMAGE CONTEXT: In Japanese beauty culture, {二|に}の{腕|うで} often appears in discussions about appearance, especially regarding concerns about arm flab ({振|ふ}り{袖|そで} - "swinging sleeves" is a slang term for flabby upper arms).

MEDICAL/ANATOMICAL TERM:
・{上腕|じょうわん} (upper arm - formal medical term)
・{上腕二頭筋|じょうわんにとうきん} (biceps)
・{上腕三頭筋|じょうわんさんとうきん} (triceps)

RELATED BODY PARTS:
・{手|て}の{甲|こう} (back of hand)
・{前腕|ぜんわん} (forearm)
・{肘|ひじ} (elbow)
・{肩|かた} (shoulder)
